messages:
incident-bot: SEV:high alert — RDMA microburst detected in cluster us-east-3 at 16:12 UTC. Multiple serving pods showing CUDA resets and container restarts. PagerDuty PD-7900. Paging @oncall-lukas and @eng-runtime-alex for triage.

sre-maya: I see sharp spike in retran_rate for ib0 on rack-r3-tor02 starting 16:11:40 UTC. P99 latency for /v1/chat jumped 3-4x. Some nodes reporting OOM kills around same time.

oncall-lukas: I'm oncall. @infra-ryan please pull switch counters and IB QP stats. @customer-success-jill please monitor customer tickets and flag high-priority accounts.

infra-ryan: pulling counters now. Observed massive Tx drops and qp_retry_exceeded on ports connected to rack-r3-tor02 -> spine-1. Link errors started right after a config push this morning (non-prod flagged) but unsure if related.

eng-runtime-alex: logs from a restarted serving container: 
``
E runtime: cuda: GPU reset detected during kernel launch
E runtime: gdr_pin failed: -110
W serving: connection to kvcache lost, requests retried
``
Also seeing `nvidia: GPU has fallen off the bus` on host dmesg. Looks like RDMA stalls provoking GDR pin failures and subsequent GPU resets.

sre-maya: kernel logs show some oom_reaper activity but mostly memory reclaim tasks. 5/64 nodes have repeated container restarts.

oncall-lukas: quick mitigation plan: 1) cordon & drain the hosts with repeated qps: gpu-us-e3-21 and gpu-us-e3-22. 2) bring ib0 down on those hosts to force TCP fallback for RDMA workloads. 3) reduce GPU-backed traffic by switching routing to cpu-fallback model. 4) throttle client retries with a short-term circuit breaker. Implementing now.

eng-runtime-alex: applying runtime gating: set route fallback for /v1/generate to `o16-cpu-fallback` and `max_inflight_per_connection=24`, `request_timeout=14s`. Also enable `kvcache_reconnect_backoff=30s` to prevent stampedes.

infra-ryan: toggled ib0 down on gpu-us-e3-21/22. After NIC down we see GPU bus errors stop on those hosts. Opening vendor TAC ticket TAC-99234; vendor acked and requested packet captures from spine and tor.

deploy-bot: deploy started: `routing/force-route` 20% traffic -> region-us-e2 (healthy) at 16:20:03 UTC.

sre-maya: autoscaler spun up +10 cpu-fallback pods in dedicated-cpu pool. Observed aggregate success rate improvement and drop in p95 for fallback routes.

customer-success-jill: two customers reported elevated 5xx/timeouts between 16:12-16:26 UTC. Both are enterprise customers; notifying account owners now.

oncall-lukas: switching to monitoring mode after immediate mitigations. Current actions: drained flapping nodes, disabled RDMA on affected hosts, routed 20% away, scaled CPU fallback, and enabled client-side circuit breaker.

infra-ryan: vendor initial analysis: microburst + ECMP path instability on spine-1 causing packet reordering and QP retries. Suggested immediate workaround: disable ECN on affected spine ports and clear ECMP hash entries to stabilize paths. Applied change at 16:34 UTC.

eng-runtime-alex: after ECN toggle and NIC down, we see request error rates fall to baseline for non-GPU routes. GPU-backed routes still show elevated tail latency; keeping routing to fallback until vendor completes trace.

ops-lead-zoe: joining. Action items for postmortem: 1) evaluate previous morning config push that may have affected ECN heuristics; 2) add alert for gdr_pin failures and `GPU has fallen off the bus` kernel lines; 3) add a runbook step to automatically reduce GPU route weight when RDMA errors cross threshold.

incident-bot: runbook prompt — start incident conference? Use /incident conference in #incident-war-room. Severity remains high (customer-impacting degraded service).

oncall-lukas: scheduling 20-min bridge and inviting vendor. @oncall-amber please prepare takeover notes.

oncall-amber: will take over after bridge. Handoff notes prep: hypothesis — network microbursts + ECMP instability -> RDMA retransmits & reorders -> GDR pin failures -> GPU bus resets -> container restarts and OOM-like symptoms. Temporary mitigations applied: NIC down, cordon/drain, traffic reroute, CPU fallback scale, circuit breakers. TAC-99234 open.

sre-maya: post-mitigation status at 16:50 UTC: 0/64 nodes flapping. Spine-1 port counters reduced significantly. Continuing to monitor for 2 hours.

customer-success-jill: sent interim status emails to affected customers with summary and ETA (vendor analysis 1-3 hours).

oncall-amber: takeover owner assigned PD-7900 -> oncall-amber; status=monitoring. Will update incident doc and file postmortem when vendor confirms root cause.

end of thread.
